findings.summary: The requirement for canonical fixed state is selected from Core collision/classification words rather than the actual placement type the host already holds.
findings.evidence: fixed_join discards entity_type from placement_fixed. It returns immediately if the Core city flag is set, and on FixedHold::Never it returns Ok when Core says not-fixed and not-of-city. Thus a real fixed-family record with no held state can be skipped using the Core collision-fixed flag instead of refusing the missing canonical state; a false CITY discriminator can bypass state for a non-CITY record. Conversely phase13 set_fixed accepts any matching placement type, rather than establishing the declared fixed-family/Movers ownership boundary. The default C reporter normally supplies state, but that does not establish missing-state or discriminator correctness at this new boundary.
findings.minimum_correction: Use actual bound placement/record family metadata to decide which properties and state the reached stage requires. At the original fixed-facts stage, an actual fixed-family placement must require canonical collision-fixed state even when its Core mirror saysfalse; only genuine CITY and non-fixed families may take their declared follow-on/no-state paths. Validate incompatible discriminators or report families by named refusal. Preserve early tallest/sector skips before fixed facts were read, direct-building/model-lookup ordering, and legitimate weapon/effect records with no fixed state. Do not add a guessed default, second pose store or query-time initialization. Extend existing real-provider tests with actual fixed-family missing state/Corefalse and non-CITY/CoreCITY cases, alongside genuine CITY/non-fixed positives.

findings.summary: The new fixed-state withdrawal is not gated by its current served-placement join, and actual failures can be mislabeled as absent coverage.
findings.evidence: candidate_question increments faults.request on a parsed non-mobile key that differs from the actually served entry, but the new fixed eligible/withdraw block checks no retained joined flag. With a live held state and a valid real need_placement reply, it can remove state for that current invalid request. The final request0 condition prevents a passing verdict, but the action itself is outside the admitted-lookup contract. Separately, the new plan.withdraw_fixed/withdrawn==0 UNREACHED return runs before checking request/reply faults or an unrelated primary failure.
findings.minimum_correction: Retain current per-question join validity and gate eligible lookup credit and real withdrawal on it before mutation. A later valid question may still be handled under the existing explicit whole-trace qualification; do not credit or mutate the invalid current one. In this new mode, report actual request/reply/unrelated-fatal failure distinctly from genuinely absent eligible lookups. Use existing positive-first driver tests for a wrong served key that real provider could otherwise answer, and failure-before-prerequisite versus honest no-prerequisite. No generic tracing framework or native bad-input run is requested.

C copies the placement key for the duration of each nonmobile offer and names every staged question by the actual sector or child placement kind. Host placement_fixed validates live key/kind, but its returned entity type is discarded by fixed_join; the resulting missing-state/discriminator authority gap is the P1 finding.

For a held state, fixed_join compares reached collision-fixed, position, shape, heading and align mirrors before using record words; the broadphase/narrowphase kernel files and original physics math are unchanged. However, the fixed-family state requirement cannot be selected from those Core mirrors: a missing state for an actual fixed-family record must not turn into a successful Core-driven skip.

The ordinary fixed constructors initialize their raw fields and attributes before insertion; phase13 is sent at the real insertion, including child-before-sector creation. Changed raw kill/unpack and bridge repair/fall/rest sites notify after the actual shape/position write. The host record follows placement LINK/lifetime rather than being repaired by a candidate question.

CITY inherits the fixed setters but is explicitly excluded by the C fixed-family reporter; its own position and box remain a declared follow-on. Fixed ALIVE was not introduced as a collision-state property. Dead structures retain collision with their actual destroyed shape. No claim of dormant unsupported readers is made.

It preserves position/heading words and validates whole shape/type and boolean fields; reply state, echoed key and zero cursor are checked in the C dialogue. The new withdrawal calls the same real provider to remove only fixed state, leaving placement and Core backing intact. NEED_PLACEMENT is a concrete C continuation, unlike the earlier post-FIRST city assumption.
